# The source-tensor regression coefficient is sharp at actual minimizers

This is an exact calibration of Section 6 of
candidate da91e18223378a53 (candidate da91e18223378a53).
It does not give a below-OC counterexample. Its budgets are at least
one half, whereas the OC constant here is one eighth.

Let `n=2,d=1`, let `P={0,1}^2`, and define

`epsilon_00=epsilon_11=1`, `epsilon_10=epsilon_01=-1`.

Fix `L>1/2` and take four unit intervals

`K_z=[epsilon_z L-1/2,epsilon_z L+1/2]`.

These are the actual integer fibers of
`C=conv union_z ({z} x K_z)`. Indeed, each binary index is an extreme
point of the cube projection, so no convex combination of other
indices changes its fiber; the cube has exactly the four binary
integer points. The hull has nonempty three-dimensional interior
because it has a two-dimensional projection and positive interval
fibers. Its source mass is `M=4`.

## 1. Exact whole-space two-cap optimum

Use exactly two continuously normalized caps. In one continuous
dimension their normals are `+1` or `-1`. A whole-line cover must
use both signs, so write the two margins as

`x-a(z)`, `b(z)-x`,

where `a,b` are affine on the base. Whole-line coverage is equivalent
to `a(z)<=b(z)` at every binary index.

The hinge of any such cover is at least `4L`. On the two positive
height fibers use `(x-a)_+>=x-a`; on the two negative height fibers
use `(b-x)_+>=b-x`, and discard the other nonnegative hinges. This gives

`Psi>=4L+sum_(epsilon=-1)b(z)-sum_(epsilon=1)a(z)`.

Since `b>=a` on each base and every affine function on the binary
square satisfies

`a(00)+a(11)=a(10)+a(01)`,

the last two sums have nonnegative difference. Thus `Psi>=4L`.

The caps `H_+={x>=0}` and `H_-={x<=0}` attain this bound. Their
source masses are each two, their hinges are each `2L`, and their
union covers the full continuous line at every base. Consequently

`v(tau)=4L` for every `tau>=1/2`.

No two-cap source cover has a budget below one half, by the elementary
union bound `M<=c_++c_-<=2tau M`. Thus this is the entire feasible
budget interval. In particular every `tau in (1/2,1)` is a regular
budget with `v'(tau)=0`.

## 2. An actual objective-one stress

For both caps set `r_i=0`. At every base take the unique whole-line
contact `x=0`, balanced weights `(lambda_+,lambda_-)=(1/2,1/2)`,
and `eta_z=1`. Both cap masses equal two. Each cap's base first
moment is `(1,1)`, which is also
`sum_z eta_z lambda_i z`. Its continuous first moment is `+2L`
or `-2L`, respectively; the contact first moments vanish. Thus

`X_i=Psi_i u_i`, `Psi_i=2L`.

These are the actual normal mass, base, and continuous moment
equations with objective multiplier one, and they satisfy exact
sensitivity `M sum_i r_i=-v'(tau)=0`. The whole-space contact lies
outside every source fiber because `L>1/2`.

## 3. Exact regression and limiting equality

The cap-plus-section source law is simply `nu=mu`, since the two
caps partition the source and the section multipliers are zero.
The normal label is `U=epsilon_z` on fiber `z`. Every affine base
feature is orthogonal to the height signs:

`sum_z epsilon_z=0`, `sum_z epsilon_z z=(0,0)`.

Therefore the least-squares continuous affine prediction from the
base is zero, including its intercept. With the notation of the
source-tensor theorem,

`A=int U^2 dnu=4`,
`Q=int xU dnu=4L=v(tau)`,
`R_x=int x^2 dnu=4L^2+1/3`.

The residual variance contribution `1/3` is four times the variance
`1/12` of a unit interval. Hence

`R_x-Q A^+ Q=1/3`,
`R_x/(Q A^+ Q)=1+1/(12L^2) -> 1` as `L -> infinity`.

This proves that the coefficient one in the positive-semidefinite
regression inequality cannot be replaced by any universal larger
coefficient, even for actual compatible mixed-integer convex fibers,
actual regular-budget hinge minimizers, exact sensitivity multipliers,
and exact zero normal and base-normal forces. A prospective sharp
budget argument must use information beyond strengthening this
covariance coefficient alone.
